conclusion: Frozen B1 retained nearly unchanged aggregate token accuracy on this one meaningful public prefix-LoRA trajectory, with local newly broken tokens and compensating improvements. Early-direction forecasts found many later failures but produced many false positives. No formal noninferiority or general fine-tuning robustness claim.

interpretation_limits: One prefix-LoRA trajectory, one base architecture/tokenizer and two fixed public domains.
Near-zero net error change does not mean individual predictions are robust.
Signed boundary analysis is retrospective and geometrically explanatory, not a prospective causal proof.
Primary failure-forecast tables condition on baseline-correct tokens; descriptive all-valid tables are separate.
Canonical dual-benchmark matrix is incomplete; no overall method ranking.
